grading_system.evidence: Total Credits Required: 22 ... For promotion ... students in grades 9-12 must accumulate the following credits ... Demonstrated Proficiency in Content Areas, 22 credits

schedule.evidence: Students in grades 9-11 must carry a minimum of 7 courses; grade 12 must carry a minimum of 6 1/2 credits per year. Courses are listed as Full Year or Semester; the catalog does not state a number of periods or a block pattern (it mentions 'period 7' and a 'Pathways Block' only).

credit_definition.text: Full-year courses carry 1 credit; semester courses carry 1/2 credit (e.g. 'Government & Civics Semester 1/2 Credit'; 'World Literature Full Year 1 Credit').
credit_definition.evidence: World Literature Full Year 1 Credit ... Wayfinding Semester 1/2 Credit

course_load.min_courses_or_credits: Grades 9-11: minimum 7 courses; grade 12: minimum 6 1/2 credits per year; exceptions in writing to Principal and Counseling Office
course_load.evidence: All students in grade 12 must carry a minimum of 6 1/2 credits per year. Students in grades 9-11 must carry a minimum of 7 courses.

local_grad_requirements.conversion_note: Catalog states requirements directly in credits (22 total: English 4.0, Performance Arts 0.5, Global Citizenship 2.5, Government 0.5, Mathematics 3.0, Science 3.0, Physical Education 1.5, Fine Arts 1.0, Health 0.5, electives balance). No conversion needed.

notes: Local requirements beyond credits: 30 hours of community service before graduation; Personalized Learning Plan (PLP) required (Act 77 of 2013); credits can be earned through proficiency in a traditional course, integrated program, or individually-designed learning experience (p.3). Promotion requires proficiency-based credit accumulation at each grade (5.5/11/16.5/22). Hazen uses the district's graduation proficiencies (p.3). Performance Arts 0.5 credit may be waived by a speaking role in three shows or presentations; PE 1.5 credits may be reduced by four high school sports seasons (1/2 credit) (p.13, p.20). Driver's Ed earns 0.5 elective credit (p.23). Some courses operate on a two-year departmental rotation (p.4).
